solution: Brute force over every bipartite graph with parts up to 5 and 4 shows the Grundy value of the delete-a-vertex-or-an-edge game is exactly ((a+b) mod 2) + 2*(|E| mod 2). Socket, moving second, wins iff the XOR over the N games is 0, i.e. iff sum(a_i+b_i) is even and an even number of graphs carry an odd edge count. The low bit is fixed by the input, so the answer is 0 when sum(a_i+b_i) is odd; otherwise the edge parities are independent and uniform, exactly half of the 2^(a_i b_i) drawings of each graph being odd, so the count is 2^(sum a_i*b_i - 1) mod 1e9+7. O(N log) time with one modular exponentiation, O(1) space.
statement_summary: Two players alternately delete one vertex or one edge from any still non-empty graph among N drawn bipartite graphs, the i-th having parts of a_i and b_i vertices, and whoever cannot move loses. The task counts, modulo 1000000007, the ways to draw the edge sets so that the second player wins under optimal play, with N up to 100000 and part sizes up to 1000000000.
notes: The Grundy formula is verified element by element (not just by value counts) on all graphs for 15 part-size pairs up to 5x2 and 4x3, and the final counting formula is verified against a full enumeration of every drawing for eleven multi-graph inputs. The formula is empirical rather than proved here, which is why confidence is 0.92 rather than higher. Statement contains no sentence addressed to the annotator.
